data.text:
Is it possible for the MCP server to ask the agent if it supports list_changed and, if so, enable soft upgrade for those agents for more features, leaving hard upgrade only for agents that don't support list_changed AND where the facade of pre-existing commands/prompts changed?

Separately, is there support in the agents to tell the MCP client to disconnect, reload the MCP server and re-connect? If that is supported, we could do soft upgrade using this capability.

data.body: Operator 2026-10-21 asked (1) can the server learn whether the client supports list_changed and widen soft upgrades for those, (2) do agents support disconnect/reload/reconnect so soft upgrade could use it. Deliverable: section in docs/ddflow/research/mcp-client-matrix.md, research notes, task edits. Also fix ruff format of the appendix python block.
data.title: Research: can the server ask the client about list_changed, and can soft upgrade ride on client reconnect

data.claim: On 2025-11-25 and earlier no negotiated field signals list_changed handling; clientInfo.name is distinctive for most clients but version is a constant for opencode ('unknown'), Qwen ('0.0.1'), Continue ('1.0.0'); on 2026-07-28 subscriptions/listen with toolsListChanged:true is an explicit opt-in.
data.falsifier: A client that sends a capability or experimental key whose presence perfectly predicts list_changed re-fetch.
data.mechanism: Legacy capabilities carry only roots/sampling/elicitation/tasks/extensions; roots.listChanged is about client roots. Qwen (ignores) and Gemini (honours) both send roots.listChanged, Cline (honours) and Roo (ignores) both send {}, so capabilities do not discriminate.
data.probe: rc.py logging stdio server run under claude -p and kilo run; spec pages fetched; client source reads at named commits
data.probe_output: claude-code 2.1.296 initialize: {"protocolVersion":"2025-11-25","capabilities":{"roots":{"listChanged":true},"elicitation":{"form":{},"url":{}}},"clientInfo":{"name":"claude-code","title":"Claude Code","version":"2.1.296"}} preceded by server/discover (2026-07-28 _meta). kilo 7.8.12: {"protocolVersion":"2025-11-25","capabilities":{"roots":{}},"clientInfo":{"name":"kilo","version":"7.8.12"}}
data.question: Can an MCP server learn at initialize whether the client re-fetches on list_changed?

data.claim: In claude -p it respawns the server lazily on the next tool call and re-runs initialize, but does NOT re-fetch tools/list (the model keeps the old tool list); an in-flight call at exit gets 'Connection closed'. A list_changed sent 0.3 s after the respawn also produced no re-fetch (one run).
data.falsifier: A tools/list request in the generation-2 log, or the model finding genN_marker for the new generation.
data.mechanism: The client reconnects the transport on demand and keeps its per-server tool cache, which only list_changed on the original connection invalidates. Docs say stdio servers are not auto-reconnected: contradicted for -p.
data.probe: claude -p --model haiku --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config cc.json --allowedTools="mcp__rc__*" -- "call whoami, die, whoami, gen2_marker"; also die_before_reply; RC_LC=1 variant
data.probe_output: whoami gen=1 pid=2101056; die ok then EXIT; whoami gen=2 pid=2112640 (log: START gen2 1.2 s after EXIT, server/discover, initialize, initialized, tools/call, no tools/list); gen2_marker not found, gen1_marker still listed. die_before_reply -> 'Connection closed', next whoami gen=2. RC_LC=1: list_changed sent at +0.3 s, no tools/list followed.
data.question: What does Claude Code 2.1.296 do when a stdio MCP server exits mid-session?

data.claim: Yes: Claude Code re-runs initialize on a new session and retries the SAME tools/call transparently within about 40 ms; the model sees no error; tools/list is not re-fetched on that connection.
data.falsifier: An error to the model on the call after expire, or no second initialize in the server log.
data.mechanism: Streamable-HTTP session-expiry handling per the spec's 404 rule.
data.probe: http_rc.py 18931 plus claude -p with a type:http mcp config: whoami, expire, whoami
data.probe_output: whoami session-gen=1; expire; whoami session-gen=3 sid changed, no error. Log: POST tools/call sid=106335 -> 404 expired; server/discover x2; initialize x2; notifications/initialized; tools/call retried with sid=480d89 (40 ms).
data.question: Does an HTTP 404 on the MCP session id make Claude Code re-initialize?

data.claim: It marks the server failed on close and drops its tools (the execute facade became unavailable in the same run), with no respawn; recovery is a manual connect (POST /mcp/:name/connect) or a network-restore event.
data.falsifier: A generation-2 START in the log after the die call, or the execute tool still available.
data.mechanism: client.onclose deletes clients/defs and publishes ToolsChanged (kilocode 5cc65d1 mcp/index.ts:555-568).
data.probe: KILO_CONFIG=kilo.json kilo run -m google/gemini-2.5-flash "call rc whoami, die, whoami"
data.probe_output: whoami gen=1; die gen=1 then EXIT; next call: Model tried to call unavailable tool 'execute'. Available tools: agent_manager_models, background_process, bash ... (no rc). No gen=2 in log. One run; idle respawn after the run not observable.
data.question: What does Kilo 7.8.12 do when a stdio MCP server exits mid-session?

data.claim: No client reacts to a server notification, exit code, SIGHUP or socket by reconnecting; respawn on exit is automatic only in Claude Code -p, VS Code (next call), OpenHands (next call), possibly Qwen (health monitor); only VS Code and Qwen re-list tools afterwards. Config-file watchers restart a server only when its entry differs.
data.falsifier: A client source path where a server-sent message or exit code triggers reconnect; or a Claude Code/OpenHands/Kimi re-list after respawn.
data.mechanism: Clients treat server death as failure and expose manual commands; reconnect paths exist for HTTP session loss (404) in Claude Code, opencode, Codex, VS Code, Kilo (patched SDK), Qwen.
data.probe: Source reads of 13 clients at pinned commits (negative greps for SIGHUP, reconnect, onclose, watch) plus the two empirical probes
data.probe_output: See docs/ddflow/research/mcp-client-matrix.md Part 2, Q2 table. Examples: gemini cleanup.ts:146 SIGHUP is shutdown; opencode index.ts:552-567 restarts only on config deep-inequality; Cline McpHub.ts:305-312 ignores non-connection field changes.
data.question: Does any MCP client let a server request disconnect/reload/reconnect, and does exit-and-respawn deliver a refreshed tool list?

data.body:
Add to each harness descriptor: list_changed = honours|ignores|unknown, verified_version, source. Seed: claude honours (2.1.296, R-soft-claude-listchanged), cursor ignores (forum 161459), others unknown (= hard). Keyed by clientInfo.name/version from the connection. A `ddflow mcp probe-client` (adapting the scratchpad srv.py) lets an operator verify any client and write the result. Prompts list_changed stays unknown until probed outside -p mode.

Client matrix (SU-client-matrix, docs/ddflow/research/mcp-client-matrix.md): seed ALL rows with evidence tag + verified_version/date, not only claude and cursor. honours: claude 2.1.296 (VERIFIED), kilo 7.8.12 (VERIFIED), opencode, gemini, vscode-copilot, cline, goose, openhands, zed (SOURCE). ignores: qwen, kimi, roo, continue, grok-cli (SOURCE), cursor-cli (REPORTED), cursor IDE unreliable (REPORTED, stdio maybe ok), codex (feature flag off by default; SOURCE). n/a: aider (no MCP). unknown: copilot-cli, antigravity, grok build, windsurf, amp, droid. Key by clientInfo.name + version range (Cursor changed between builds). Add a tri-state source: verified|source|reported|observed (learned at runtime by SU-announce's acknowledgement wait). Unknown = hard. Only additions/removals count as honoured: Claude Code does not adopt a changed schema of a loaded tool. prompts/list_changed is never relied on.

Reconnect pass (SU-reconnect-research, docs/ddflow/research/mcp-client-matrix.md Part 2): (1) clientInfo.version is NOT reliable: opencode sends 'unknown', Qwen a constant '0.0.1', Continue a constant '1.0.0' (SOURCE) - key those by name alone and mark entries expiring; version ranges only for claude-code, kilo, gemini-cli-mcp-client, codex-mcp-client, Zed, Goose. Seed the exact clientInfo.name strings from the Part 2 table. (2) Add columns: reconnect = respawn+relist | respawn | manual | none (Claude Code -p respawns but does NOT re-list, VERIFIED; VS Code respawns on next call and re-lists; Qwen health monitor re-lists, stdio exit detection UNKNOWN; Kilo/opencode drop tools and need a manual connect), http_404 = reinit+retry | none, and listen_optin (2026-07-28 subscriptions/listen toolsListChanged seen). (3) Capabilities do not discriminate honouring clients, do not use them.

On a swap whose digest changed: set listChanged true for tools and prompts; emit notifications/tools/list_changed and prompts/list_changed on legacy revisions, serve subscriptions/listen on 2026-07-28 (opt-in types), and replace the fixed 1 h tools/list ttlMs with a short one plus the digest so cached lists converge. Debounce and coalesce. Only when the client is known to honour it (SU-client-table); else classify hard.

Client matrix: (1) only tools/list_changed is announced for correctness; prompts/resources are best effort (few clients re-list prompts). (2) Observed acknowledgement: after sending list_changed the shim waits N s for a tools/list from that client; a re-fetch records the (clientInfo name, version) as honours/observed in the client table, silence records ignores and returns a hard verdict with the restart notice (SU-restart-notice). (3) 2026-07-28 clients (Codex/Goose/opencode can negotiate it): short ttlMs keyed to the digest. (4) Cline answers by restarting its session, so debounce/coalesce bursts.

Depends in practice on SU-client-table for the honours/ignores verdict.

Reconnect pass: on 2026-07-28 a connection that sent subscriptions/listen with toolsListChanged:true IS a negotiated 'honours' signal (spec), and the server must not send unrequested notification types: serve listen and ack the subset (DOCS subscriptions page); legacy revisions have no such signal. Do NOT use a handshake probe (list_changed right after initialized with no change) as a gate: on Claude Code's respawned connection it produced no tools/list (one run, cause UNKNOWN), so it false-negatives; a probe result may only be stored as 'probe-silent'. Observation state machine: unknown -> honours(observed) after one tools/list re-fetch within 10 s; unknown -> ignores(observed) only after two silent notifications in different sessions; a later re-fetch overrides. Debounce knowledge: Cline 300 ms/2 s, opencode 100 ms.

After `ddflow upgrade --apply` (and on the periodic stale check) classify with SU-digest and act: SOFT -> swap the worker and print 'soft upgrade applied, no restart needed (interface unchanged | N tools added, M removed: announced to <client>)'; HARD -> 'hard upgrade: restart your agent' with the reason (shim changed / protocol changed / client <name> does not refresh tools). New [mcp].upgrade = soft|notify|off, default soft where classification allows; keep on_upgrade=reexec as the hard-upgrade path that avoids a client reconnect when the shim itself is stable. doctor shows running vs installed versions, class of the pending upgrade, client capability. Same text on CLI, MCP footer and the SessionStart hook.

Rule (docs/ddflow/research/mcp-client-matrix.md): SOFT iff digest unchanged OR (change is additive/removal AND client honours list_changed: table verified/source or observed ack) OR facade mode on (SU-facade-mode; the digest then covers only the facade tools + instructions). A schema change of an existing tool is soft only with the worker grace (previous schema accepted for one version) AND an honouring client; else HARD. Otherwise HARD with the reason naming the client. The report names the mode used (unchanged | announced to <client> | facade). Needs SU-facade-mode and SU-restart-notice.

Refined rule (Part 2 of the matrix doc, proposal pending SU-decision): 1 soft silent (digest unchanged, or facade on); 2 soft announced (additive/removal/compatible schema AND client honours: table, listen opt-in, or observed); 3 soft with features pending (additive/removal and client ignores/unknown: old tools keep working, removed tools served one more version, report 'N new tools appear after you restart the agent'; unknown clients are still announced and observed); 4 soft via reconnect (reexec) only for a client the table marks respawn+relist, reporting that one in-flight call may fail; 5 HARD only when a tool/prompt the client already holds changes incompatibly and the client does not honour list_changed or does not adopt schema changes (Claude Code, VERIFIED) and no facade/grace, or the shim/protocol changed. Report names the rung used.

Present R-soft-* and the recommendation; settle: (1) A+D over B/C-only, (2) worker transport: stdio pipes to a child (default, portable incl. Windows) vs unix socket, (3) the soft/hard definition in the phase body, (4) schema grace: worker accepts the previous schema's arguments for one version, (5) what happens for clients that ignore list_changed (hard, tell the user). Record with ddflow decision add --globs ddflow/mcpshim/**,ddflow/surfaces/mcp*.py. Do not start SU-shim before this is decided.

Item (5) revised by the client matrix: clients that ignore list_changed are not simply hard. Decide: facade mode (ddflow_search/ddflow_call, MTD-search-call) as the way to make upgrades soft for them, the per-call restart notice as the fallback, and the rule 'soft iff digest unchanged OR client honours OR facade on'. See docs/ddflow/research/mcp-client-matrix.md.

Operator questions 2026-10-21 (recorded verbatim in the session log) answered in docs/ddflow/research/mcp-client-matrix.md Part 2. Decide additionally: (6) identify by table + listen opt-in + observation (SU-observe-client-capability), no handshake probe; (7) adopt the 5-rung soft/hard rule in SU-upgrade-integration, in particular rung 3 'soft with features pending' (an additive change is soft for every client) and the operator's split 'hard only when no list_changed AND the pre-existing facade changed incompatibly'; (8) reconnect is a fallback tier only (SU-reconnect-fallback): no client lets a server request a reconnect, exit-and-respawn drops the in-flight call and most clients keep the stale list (R-soft-cc-stdio-respawn, R-soft-reconnect-source-matrix).

After an announced change, wait up to 10 s for tools/list on the same connection and record the result per client key (clientInfo.name, plus version only where the table says it is meaningful) in a local file (.ddflow/local/mcp-clients.json). State machine: unknown -> honours(observed) on one re-fetch; unknown -> ignores(observed) after two silent notifications in different sessions; re-fetch overrides silence; entries carry date and version, expire on version change or after N upgrades; a VERIFIED/SOURCE table row is never overwritten, a contradiction is logged as a defect. A 2026-07-28 connection that opened subscriptions/listen with toolsListChanged:true is recorded honours(listen) at once. No handshake probe as a gate (false negative measured: R-soft-cc-stdio-respawn). Tests: simulated honouring, lazy, debouncing (Cline 300 ms) and silent clients; the cache survives a shim restart. Research: docs/ddflow/research/mcp-client-matrix.md Part 2, R-soft-initialize-signals.
data.title: Learn list_changed handling per client at runtime: observation cache plus 2026-07-28 listen opt-in

data.body: No client lets a server request a reconnect (R-soft-reconnect-source-matrix) and exit-and-respawn fails the in-flight call; Claude Code -p respawns lazily but keeps the stale tool list (VERIFIED). So reconnect is rung 4 only: the existing [mcp].on_upgrade=reexec is chosen instead of the restart notice when the table marks the client reconnect=respawn+relist; the report says one in-flight call may fail. Work: (1) run Qwen Code (and VS Code if available) against docs appendix B probe rc.py to learn whether a stdio exit is noticed and tools are re-listed, fill the table; (2) the policy and report text; (3) never reexec when the shim connection is stable. Decide in SU-decision whether to keep it at all: if Qwen does not notice stdio exits the tier has no member and this task is dropped.
data.title: Reconnect as a fallback soft tier: reexec only for clients that respawn and re-list; verify Qwen
